**Chapter 10: Mineral Resources: Metal-Nonmetal**

**Section 10.1: Reactivity Series of Metal**

| **Metal's Position in the Reactivity Series** | **Metal** | **Reduction Method** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Highly reactive metals at the top rankings | K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al | Reduction is done through Electrolysis |
| Medium standard reactive metals at the mid level rankings | Zn, Fe, Pb | Reduction is done through Carbon Reduction |
| Less reactive metals at the bottom rankings | Cu, Hg, Ag | Reduction is done through Self Reduction |
| Non-reactive metals at the fag end of rankings | Pt, Au | Found in pure form |

**Reduction by Electrolysis:**

The top ranking metals in the reactivity series like K, Na, Ca, Mg and Al undergo reduction by electrolysis. The Aluminum extraction from Aluminum oxide by electrolysis is described below.

Solid aluminum oxide needs to be melted into liquid first. Aluminum oxide melts at 2050°C. To raise the temperature so high is very tough. If aluminum oxide is added with cryolite (Na3AlF6), it melts at 800°C-1000°C. The melted Al2O3 consists of Al3+ and O2- ion.

Al2O3 → 2Al3+ + 3O2-

A steel container with graphite carbon layer is necessary in the method. The mixture of aluminum oxide and cryolite is taken in the container and some carbon rods are dipped in the mixture in a way so that they do not touch the steel container. **Answer Key:**

(a) The reactivity series of metal is: K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Pb, Cu, Hg, Ag, Pt, Au

(b) Reduction is done through Electrolysis

(c) Reduction is done through Carbon Reduction

(d) Reduction is done through Self Reduction

(e) Found in pure form

(f) 2050°C

(g) It melts at 800°C-1000°C

(h) Al3+ and O2-

(i) To prevent the carbon rods from touching the steel container

(j) To connect the steel container to the negative charge
